articles.title: First Grader Khalib, 7, Goes on a Bird Walk with His Conservation Scientist Hero
articles.summary: Seven-year-old Khalib Townsend dreams of becoming a conservation scientist. With help from his mom and NPR, he met his hero, Keith Russell, for a rainy bird walk in Philadelphia. Russell shared his own path from first-grade bird lover to Audubon scientist.

articles.title: PM Burnham Vows 'Relentless' Action as Small Boat Crossings Surge Past 2,000
articles.summary: New UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham pledged to be 'relentless' in curbing small boat crossings after 326 people arrived on Saturday alone. The government has nearly doubled the number of officers targeting smuggling gangs and seized equipment that could have aided 72,000 illegal entries.

articles.title: Fields Turn to Dust: UK Drought Threatens Food Supply and Farmers' Livelihoods
articles.summary: Parched fields in Northamptonshire tell a grim story: the UK's worst drought in years is slashing crop yields and forcing livestock farmers to dip into winter feed. NFU president Tom Bradshaw warns of potential food shortages and calls for urgent investment in water security.
